**Title** (new)
Report delivery: emailed and downloaded reports arrive empty, short, duplicated, or misdated

**Body** (as-new)

```markdown
## Context

A customer support review triggered this ask. Today a report can be downloaded or emailed.

## Problem

The first download from an emailed report is empty, so recipients waste a retry.
Example (empty first download): a 12-row report downloaded as zero rows, and a later retry gave 12 rows.

Downloads drop the final row, so recipients get incomplete totals.
Example (missing final row): a four-row report downloaded as three rows, while all four rows showed on screen.

One delivery sends the email twice, so recipients have to check whether the two reports differ.
Example (duplicate email): one delivery request sent two emails with the same file.

The email subject names the previous day's report, so recipients misfile today's work.
Example (wrong subject date): an October 21 request produced an October 20 subject, though the file itself was dated October 21.

## Idea

The reporter proposes fixing report delivery so that each request sends one email carrying a complete, correctly dated report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given an emailed 12-row report, when the recipient downloads it for the first time, the download contains 12 rows.
- [ ] Given a four-row report, when it is downloaded, the file contains all four rows shown on screen.
- [ ] Given one delivery request, when the report is emailed, exactly one email is sent.
- [ ] Given a report requested on October 21, when it is emailed, the email subject names October 21.
```

**Metadata changeset**
- `type: (unset) -> bug` -- the ticket reports four observed delivery defects. No other fields were gathered.

**Evidence**
All four items were supplied by the reporter in the ask. No environment or date was recorded, and no screenshot, log, or link was supplied.
- Empty first download. Observed: the first download of an emailed 12-row report had zero rows, and a later retry had 12. Expected: 12 rows on the first download.
- Missing final row. Observed: a four-row report downloaded as three rows, while four showed on screen. Expected: four rows in the download.
- Duplicate email. Observed: one delivery request sent two emails with the same file. Expected: one email.
- Wrong subject date. Observed: an October 21 request had an October 20 subject, though the file was dated October 21. Expected: the subject names October 21.

The four source gaps are listed above the Title. You can approve the write despite them.

**Roast dispositions**
- Applied: the mechanism explanation and the internal identifiers (`deliveryMux`, `writeRows`, `sendMail`) were moved out of Context and into the Reporter note verbatim. Context and Problem keep only product-level cause and effect.
- Surfaced as ambiguous: none.

**Split**
Not proposed. The four failures were observed independently, but no evidence was supplied that they could ship separately, so no split axis is established. This stays one ticket, as the default.

**Proposed comment** (posted after the body; one approval covers title, body, metadata, and this comment)

```text
Reporter note: the export job writes CSV through the mail queue before the row count is known; deliveryMux calls writeRows then sendMail.
```

**Title — as new:** Fix report downloads and delivery emails

## Body — as new

### Context

A customer support review prompted this request to fix report delivery. Reports can currently be downloaded or emailed.

### Problem

The first download from a report email can be empty, forcing recipients to retry.

**First emailed download:** A 12-row report initially downloads as zero rows; retrying later returns all 12 rows.

Downloads can omit the final row, leaving recipients with incomplete totals.

**Final download row:** A four-row report downloads as three rows even though the fourth row appears on screen.

A single delivery request can send duplicate emails, making recipients check whether the reports differ.

**Duplicate email:** One delivery request sends two emails containing the same file.

The email subject can name yesterday’s report, causing recipients to misfile today’s work.

**Email subject date:** An October 21 request produces an October 20 subject even though the attached file is October 21.

### Idea

The reporter proposes fixing report delivery so downloaded reports and delivery emails match the requested report.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a 12-row report requested by email, when the recipient first downloads it from the email, the download contains all 12 rows without a retry.
- [ ] Given a four-row report whose fourth row appears on screen, when the report is downloaded, the download contains all four rows.
- [ ] Given one report-delivery request, when email delivery completes, the recipient receives exactly one email for that request.
- [ ] Given an October 21 report request whose file is dated October 21, when its delivery email is sent, the subject names October 21.

## Metadata changeset

## Evidence

These are reporter-supplied observations; no links, attachments, or screenshots were supplied.

| first emailed download | Request a 12-row report by email and download it; retry later. | First download has zero rows; retry has 12. | First download has 12 rows. |
| final download row | Download a report showing four rows on screen. | Download has three rows. | Download has all four rows. |
| duplicate email | Make one report-delivery request. | Two emails contain the same file. | One email is sent. |
| email subject date | Request the October 21 report and inspect the email subject and file date. | Subject names October 20; file is October 21. | Subject names October 21. |
